reason: The text explicitly narrates the Golden Calf incident (Exodus 32), where the Israelites demonstrate profound ingratitude to both their leaders and Yahweh. When Moses delays descending from Mount Sinai, the people gather and tell Aaron, 'Rise up, make us gods who shall go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt—we do not know what has become of him' (לֹא יָדַעְנוּ מֶה־ הָיָה לוֹ). This represents abandonment of Moses despite his leadership. Simultaneously, despite having just witnessed God's power and agreed to Yahweh's covenant ('all that the Lord has spoken we will do'), they fashion a golden calf and declare it as their god. Moses explicitly characterizes this as 'a great sin' (חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה), and the narrative clearly presents this as an act of rebellion and ingratitude toward both their leader and their God, violating the covenant they had just ratified.
